sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,650.50, almost exactly mid-range (50%) of its trailing one-month band between 7,551.81 and 7,747.71. The Nasdaq 100 closed at 29,644.17, right at the top of its own one-month range, while the Euro Stoxx 50 sits at the bottom of its band at 6,236.20. The VIX at 14.81 is near the low end of its recent range, consistent with a calm volatility backdrop heading into the week. This week's earnings load is heavier than usual — 23 SP500/R1000/core reports, with industrials (six names) the most represented sector, followed by technology, consumer-defensive and consumer-cyclical (three each).

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Mon: JEF US reports into a subdued financial-services cluster, median +0.2% on recent prints. Tue: HXL US reports into industrials, the week's most-represented sector and running cool at a median -1.4% across 627 names. Wed: MU US and FDS US both report — Micron sits in technology's modest +0.9% median, while FactSet is back in the same soft financial-services read as JEF. Thu: ACN US reports into that same +0.9% technology cluster, one of the sector's bigger prints of the week. Fri closes the week with KO US, reporting into a consumer-defensive group running slightly negative at -0.6% median.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the reaction table this cycle at +6.6% median across 176 tickers, backed by a thick 2,630-item news window. Alternative-asset-management (+2.9%, 6 names) and copper (+2.6%, 6 names) trail close behind on much thinner coverage. Oil-gas is the outlier in the other direction, down -2.5% median across 33 names on a comparably thick 1,021-item window.
